description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Representative Jill Tokuda (D-HI), warns Taiwan "must not be a bargaining chip" during President Donald Trump's talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Tom Kloza, Chief Energy Advisor at Gulf Oil, says reopening the Strait of Hormuz is "the only lever you can pull that has a major impact" on fuel prices, warning gasoline could reach $5 a gallon or higher this summer if it stays closed. Mara Rudman, Professor at the University of Virginia's Miller Center and former Deputy Envoy for Middle East Peace at the US State Department, says there is likely no "near-term" diplomatic solution with Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US-Iran Tensions Flare Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting | Balance of Power: Late Edition 05/11/2026

author: Niki Koswanage, Tom Redmond
description: Malaysia’s anti-graft chief Azam Baki is poised to end his six-year run with two investigations relating to him and the agency still pending.
title: Malaysia’s Anti-Graft Chief Ends Term With Probes Unresolved

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: Kevin Warsh’s nomination to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors on Monday cleared the first in a series of Senate votes planned this week to install him as chair of the US central bank.
title: Warsh’s Fed Nomination Clears First in Series of Senate Votes

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: US House lawmakers asked Jes Staley, a former top executive at Barclays Plc and  JPMorgan Chase & Co., for an interview in its ongoing probe into disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein.
title: Jes Staley Asked to Sit for US House Interview Over Epstein Ties

author: Michael Shepard, Maggie Eastland, Jeff Mason
description: The roster of business leaders invited to join President Donald Trump on his trip to China this week left off one notable, and surprising, name: Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
title: Nvidia’s CEO to Miss China Trip After Year of Travels With Trump

description: Bloomberg's Devika Krishna Kumar breaks down the latest movement in the oil markets as Trump throws cold water on hopes of a deal between the US and Iran. Then, Hardika Singh, economic strategist at Fundstrat, discusses the markets as stocks continue to trade higher despite risk from the war in Iran. Plus, Bloomberg Economics chief geoeconomics analyst Jennifer Welch previews Trump's trip to Beijing to meet with China's President Xi later this week. Finally, Angi CEO Jeff Kip talks his company's 'radical pivot' to AI. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Gains as Trump Signals Iran Deal On 'Life Support' | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/11/2026

description: Mara Rudman, Professor at the University of Virginia's Miller Center and former Deputy Envoy for Middle East Peace at the US State Department, says there is likely no "near-term" diplomatic solution with Iran. She argues the US is "further away" from addressing Iran's nuclear program than it was under the Obama-era deal. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: No 'Magic Bullet' in Iran War: Rudman

description: Tom Kloza, Chief Energy Advisor at Gulf Oil, says reopening the Strait of Hormuz is "the only lever you can pull that has a major impact" on fuel prices, warning gasoline could reach $5 a gallon or higher this summer if it stays closed. He says pausing federal gasoline taxes would have limited impact and could be difficult to reinstate once halted. Kloza also cautions hurricane disruptions could push prices to "an apoplectic level." He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Strait 'Only Lever' on Gas Prices: Kloza

author: Liam Knox
description: The number of new foreign undergraduate students at US colleges dropped by an average of 20% this spring from a year earlier, according to a study by a coalition of education groups, the latest sign that President Donald Trump’s standoff with higher education is hammering a key source of talent and funding.
title: US Colleges Report 20% Drop in Foreign Students Over Visa Clampdown

author: Will Kubzansky
description: A federal gasoline tax holiday as proposed by President Donald Trump would result in billions of dollars in lost tax revenue each month, independent budget analysts say.
title: Trump’s Gas Tax Holiday Would Cost $3.5 Billion a Month

description: Representative Jill Tokuda (D-HI), a member of the House Armed Services Committee and House China Select Committee, warns Taiwan "must not be a bargaining chip" during President Donald Trump's talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping. She says Beijing “has been watching” US military deployments, arguing that the Iran conflict has put America in a “weakened position” ahead of talks. Rep. Tokuda also says the war "has never stopped" despite ceasefire claims and pushes for another congressional war powers vote when the House and Senate return next week. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Taiwan 'Not a Bargaining Chip:' Rep. Tokuda

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the White House. On today's show, American Enterprise Institute Nonresident Senior Fellow Heather Conley, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Principal Cyber Advisor to the Secretary of the Army Brandon Pugh. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Ceasefire Is Weakened | Balance of Power: Early Edition 05/11/2026

author: Ari Natter
description: US President Donald Trump has mounted a new push to tackle affordability, taking aim at beef and gasoline amid surging consumer prices that may threaten his party’s hold on Congress.
title: Trump Takes Aim at Beef, Fuel Prices as Inflation Risks Mount

author: Olesia Safronova
description: Ukraine’s anti-graft authorities have accused President Volodymyr Zelenskiy’s former top aide of money-laundering, according to a statement on Monday.
title: Zelenskiy’s Former Top Aide Is Accussed of Money-Laundering

description: Bill Rauch and Zhailon Levingston, co-directors of CATS: The Jellicle Ball, said that the story of CATS makes sense as iconic characters moving through the Harlem ballroom scene. Rauch and Levingston discuss how they brought the musical, which reimagines the classic Andrew Lloyd Weber musical, to life and how the story maps onto a new cultural context. Bloomberg Pursuits editor-at-large Chris Rovzar shared his experience with the show.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: CATS: The Jellicle Ball Brings Ballroom Culture to Broadway

author: Swati Pandey
description: Australia’s center-left government is expected to crack down on tax concession for property investors as part of efforts to ease generational inequality and help rein in a budget deficit.
title: Australia to Tackle Housing Tax as Budget Deficit Set to Narrow

author: Lauren Rosenthal, Zahra Hirji
description: The Trump administration selected Cameron Hamilton to lead the Federal Emergency Management Agency, which is grappling with reduced staffing levels ahead of hurricane season in the Atlantic.
title: Trump Taps Former FEMA Chief Hamilton to Lead Agency Again

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: The Pentagon’s leadership is now supportive of the Navy’s next-generation stealth fighter replacing the service’s aging F/A-18 Super Hornet, after previously pushing back against the new program.
title: Pentagon ‘Committed’ to Navy’s New Stealth F/A-XX Warplane

author: Dan Williams
description: Israel’s parliament approved a special military tribunal for hundreds of Palestinians accused of taking part in the attacks in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, some of whom could face execution.
title: Israel Will Prosecute Oct. 7 Suspects in Eichmann-Style Tribunal

author: Nancy Cook
description: The president floats suspending the federal levy as the conflict drags on.
title: What Trump’s Gas Tax Plan Says About the War With Iran

author: Greg Stohr
description: Virginia asked the US Supreme Court to reinstate a new voter-approved congressional map that was designed to flip four Republican-held House seats in the November election.
title: Virginia Asks US Supreme Court to Restore Democrat-Friendly Map

author: Anthony Capaccio, Roxana Tiron
description: The US Navy said it plans to buy at least 15 new battleships endorsed by President Donald Trump over the next 30 years, according to its new shipbuilding plan, marking a deeper commitment than previously revealed to what could be the costliest warship ever produced.
title: Navy Plans to Buy 15 Costly Trump-Class Battleships by 2055

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The Trump administration asked the US trade court to pause a ruling that declared the president’s latest 10% global tariffs unlawful while the government appeals, meaning importers would keep paying the levies while the legal fight continues.
title: US Asks to Keep Collecting Trump’s New Tariffs After Court Loss

description: Brandon Pugh, Principal Cyber Advisor to the Secretary of the Army joins to discuss the current state of cyber security in the US. As well as the the importance of being on the cutting edge of cyber research.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Protecting The US Against Cyber Threats Is a 'No Fail' Mission, Says Pugh

description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said he will not resign during a televised address to the nation on Monday. “To do so would be to give credence to a panel report that unfortunately has grave flaws,” he said. An independent panel found Ramaphosa may be guilty of serious misconduct in relation to the theft of money at his game farm. (Corrects spelling of Ramaphosa)
title: South Africa’s Ramaphosa Says He Won’t Resign

description: Heather Conley, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute, said President Trump goes into his summit in China this week in a weakened position because of the continuing standoff with Iran after he rejected Tehran’s latest peace offer. She also discussed the Ukraine ceasefire and what this means for the future for the region.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: America's Capability and Creditably as An Ally Is Being Tested Says Conley

author: S'thembile Cele, Ntando Thukwana
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said he would contest a report over his handling of a robbery at his farm after a court ruling resurrected the scandal, and rejected calls that he step down.
title: Ramaphosa Says Won’t Resign Over Court Ruling, Denies Wrongdoing

author: Zach C Cohen, Maeve Sheehey
description: House Speaker Mike Johnson and the head of the Secret Service will meet with Senate Republicans Tuesday as lawmakers consider legislation giving that agency $1 billion to make security improvements tied to the White House ballroom.
title: Secret Service, House Speaker to Talk Trump Ballroom Funding With Senate GOP

author: Jan Bratanic
description: Slovenian lawmakers aligned with nationalist leader Janez Jansa pushed through a series of legislative amendments that critics say favor the Alpine country’s rich.
title: Slovenia’s Nationalist Leader Backs Legislation Critics Say Favors Rich

author: Ilena Peng, Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump will sign two executive orders Monday to try to lower beef prices, according to a White House official, the latest effort by the administration to counter high consumer prices ahead of November midterms.
title: Trump to Sign Orders Monday Aimed at Lowering Beef Prices

author: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan, Joe Mayes
description: Allies of UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting joined the growing calls for Keir Starmer to step down as pressure mounted on the prime minister in the wake of last week’s disastrous local election results.
title: Streeting Allies Urge Starmer to Go as Pressure on Premier Grows

description: President Donald Trump said he will discuss US arms sales to Taiwan with Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a meeting this week. “I’m going to have that discussion,” Trump said. “President Xi would like us not to. And I’ll have that discussion.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He'll Talk About Selling Arms to Taiwan at Xi Summit

author: Catherine Lucey
description: US President Donald Trump said he is satisfied with the government’s response to the recent hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship, stating that the virus is “not easy to spread.”
title: Trump Downplays Hantavirus Concern, Says ‘Not Easy to Spread’

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: US President Donald Trump reiterated that he would raise the case of imprisoned Hong Kong businessman Jimmy Lai when he meets Chinese leader Xi Jinping at their summit this week.
title: Trump Vows to Discuss Case of Imprisoned Jimmy Lai With Xi

author: Yash Roy
description: Sean Duffy taped a reality TV show while leading the US Transportation Department, raising concerns about corporate sponsorships of the show from companies that are overseen by his department.
title: Sean Duffy’s Reality Show Draws Ethics Concerns Over Sponsorships

description: President Donald Trump said the ceasefire between the US and Iran was on “massive life support” after he rejected Tehran’s latest peace offer. He speaks to reporters in the Oval Office. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says Iran Ceasefire Is on 'Life Support'

author: Kate Sullivan, Salma El Wardany, Galit Altstein
description: The ceasefire between the US and Iran reached a particularly precarious moment Monday as President Donald Trump said the agreement was on “massive life support” after he rejected Tehran’s latest peace offer.
title: Trump Says US-Iran Ceasefire on ‘Massive Life Support’

author: Curtis Heinzl
description: Canadian travel to the US posted its first increase since the end of 2024, though the rebound is modest and largely reflects a comparison with low cross-border trips last year.
title: US Travel by Canadians Sees First Gain Since December 2024

author: Rene Vollgraaff
description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa will address the nation following the judgment of the Constitutional Court in the case brought by the Economic Freedom Fighters challenging the National Assembly’s decision with respect to Section 89 proceedings, his office said in an emailed statement.
title: South Africa’s Ramaphosa to Address the Nation at 8pm

author: Courtney McBride
description: A bipartisan group of senators has urged President Donald Trump to advance a $14 billion arms sale for Taiwan and signal to Chinese leader Xi Jinping at a summit in Beijing this week that US support for the island nation is non-negotiable.
title: Senators Push Trump on Taiwan Arms Package Ahead of Xi Summit

author: Caitlin Reilly
description: President Donald Trump voiced support for a gasoline tax holiday to counter rising prices at the pump, as the cost of oil soars while the war with Iran drags on.
title: Trump Floats Temporary Gas Tax Halt as Pump Prices Soar

author: Jeff Mason
description: The White House is inviting Tesla Inc.’s Elon Musk, Apple Inc.’s Tim Cook and Boeing Co.’s Kelly Ortberg and executives from other large companies to accompany President Donald Trump on his trip to China this week, according to an official.
title: Musk, Cook Set to Join Trump for Xi Summit, White House Says

author: Gerry Doyle
description: As long as the Strait of Hormuz remains unsettled, the US Navy faces millions of dollars in extra costs each time it sends a destroyer through the waterway, and such passages on their own are unlikely to reopen it.
title: US Navy Faces Rising Costs for Hormuz Missions With Strait Still Blocked

description:
Keir Starmer vowed to prove his critics wrong in a speech to save his premiership following bruising local elections.

Lizzy Burden explains how the markets reacted. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Starmer Fights To Save His Premiership

author: Paul Richardson
description: A scandal that led South African President Cyril Ramaphosa to consider resigning four years ago has come back to haunt him.
title: How Cash-in-a-Sofa Scandal Threatens to Topple South Africa’s Ramaphosa

author: Sara Sjolin
description: One of the world’s largest commodity shipping companies is planning for a scenario in which the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively shut for the rest of the year, highlighting how the Iran conflict is upending expectations across the maritime cargo industry.
title: Norden Is Assuming Its Ships Will Be Stuck in Hormuz All Year

author: Catherine Lucey
description: The Trump administration is still working through its plans for oversight of cutting-edge AI models, but doesn’t envision a big new agency for the job, according to White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett.
title: No New Bureaucracy to Police AI Products, Hassett Says

author: Alice Gledhill, James Hirai
description: UK government bonds slid as calls grew for UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer to step aside following his party’s large losses in local elections last week.
title: Gilts Slide as Calls Grow for UK Prime Minister to Step Down

author: S'thembile Cele
description: South Africa’s speaker of parliament will submit an advisory report that will form the basis of an impeachment committee’s investigation into President Cyril Ramaphosa when lawmakers meet on Tuesday.
title: South African Parliament Prepares to Initiate Ramaphosa Inquiry

author: Chris Strohm
description: The man accused of trying to assassinate President Donald Trump at a Washington hotel gala last month pleaded not guilty during a hearing in federal court Monday.
title: Gala Shooting Suspect Pleads Not Guilty to Trying to Kill Trump

author: Anup Roy, Ruchi Bhatia, Shruti Srivastava
description: India is considering emergency steps to shore up foreign-exchange reserves, including curbing non-essential imports like gold and electronic goods, and hiking fuel prices, to help cushion the economy from the fallout of the Iran war, people familiar with the matter said.
title: India Considering Emergency Measures to Save Foreign Exchange

author: Neil Jerome Morales
description: A Philippine lawmaker, linked to a human rights case before the International Criminal Court, was chased through the hall of the Senate on Monday by authorities, a bizarre sideshow to the drama playing out between President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his vice-president, and arch-nemesis, Sara Duterte.
title: Agents Chase Philippine Senator Tied to ICC Case Amid Duterte Impeachment Chaos

author: Andrea Palasciano
description: The European Union reached a political agreement to sanction violent settlers in the West Bank, marking the first time the bloc has been able to get unanimous backing for punitive measures against Israel since the height of the Gaza crisis.
title: EU Backs Sanctions on Violent Israeli Settlers in the West Bank

author: Simon Marks
description: Drone strikes have killed at least 880 civilians in Sudan this year, with the civil war likely to widen in the coming weeks and put non-combatants further at risk, the United Nations said.
title: Drone Strikes Kill Nearly 900 Sudan Civilians This Year, UN Says

author: Colum Murphy
description: China’s industrial strategy threatens hundreds of billions of dollars worth of industrial output in the world’s most advanced economies, posing a danger of hollowing out their industrial capabilities, according to a release from the largest American business lobby.
title: China’s Policies Threaten $650 Billion in G-7, US Chamber Says

author: Ewa Krukowska
description: The European Commission put forward updated benchmark values for its flagship carbon market in a bid to address concerns among some governments and manufacturers over the region’s declining competitiveness.
title: EU Proposes Changes to Free Emission Permits to Appease Industry

description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he'd contest any leadership challenge, as he battled to save his premiership following bruising local elections. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Starmer Vows to Prove Critics Wrong in Speech to Save Job

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: The president prepares for his Xi summit amid swirling conflicts and ceasefires tied to Beijing’s allies
title: Trump’s China Trip Reflects Second Term Focus Abroad

description:
Former French Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire argued that Europe urgently needs a stronger more competitive economy and that companies like TotalEnergies should not be more taxed because they benefit from higher oil prices.

He also warned about far-left extremism in France, one year ahead of the French presidential elections. Le Maire spoke exclusively with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua from London. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: France’s Le Maire: Europe Needs Urgent Economic Reset

description: Latvia will work with Ukraine and its allies to better handle defense against drones that stray into its territory, Latvian Foreign Minister Baiba Braze said, after two drones crashed last week in the country’s east, forcing Defense Minister Andris Spruds to resign late on Sunday. Braze spoke to BTV's Oliver Crook on Monday ahead of the Foreign Affairs Council in Brussels. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Latvia to Work on Drone Defense with Ukraine, Says Foreign Minister

description: Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said that Vilnius welcomes US troops “wherever they are” on the continent, though said the closer those forces are to Russia the more effective their role in deterrence. He made the comments in an interview with BTV's Oliver Crook on Monday morning, ahead of the Foreign Affairs Council in Brussels. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lithuania 'Welcomes' US Troops, Says Foreign Minister

description: Jane Foley, head of FX strategy at Rabobank, discusses the outlook for gilt markets as UK Prime Minister attempts to persuade the Labour Party that he is the right person to lead it following last week's heavy losses in local election results. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Starmer's UK Leadership Woes Add to Gilt Risks, Rabobank Says

author: Zoltan Simon, Marton Kasnyik
description: The new government of Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar is risking a standoff with the European Union over a plan to stick with Russian energy purchases.
title: Hungary’s New Government Risks EU Fight Over Russian Energy

author: Sanne Wass
description: The head of Denmark’s Liberal party said he has a two-week deadline to form the country’s new government, after record-long talks were thrown off track last week.
title: Danish Liberal Leader Gets Two Weeks to Try to Form a Government

author: S'thembile Cele
description: A scandal has resurfaced involving a concealed hoard of dollars at the South African president’s ranch.
title: The Unlikely Scandal Tripping Up Ramaphosa

description:
UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, in a speech aimed at re-setting his premiership, says he takes responsibility for the governing Labour Party's performance in last week's local elections. "I know I have my doubters, and I know I need to prove them wrong, and I will," Starmer adds.
 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: UK's Starmer Says He Will Prove His 'Doubters' Wrong

author: Alex Wickham, Ellen Milligan, Joe Mayes
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said he won’t abandon the responsibility of leading the country, as he battled to save his premiership in a make-or-break speech.
title: Starmer Vows to Prove His Critics Wrong in Speech to Save Job

author: Marcelo Rochabrun, Carla Samon Ros
description: Fewer than 15,000 votes stand between a leftist representing Peru’s impoverished communities and a conservative hotel magnate who represents the capital city as they compete for the final spot in June’s presidential runoff.
title: Stark Class Divides Are Deepening Peru’s Electoral Chaos

author: Stephen Stapczynski
description: Another tanker loaded with liquefied natural gas from Qatar is nearing the Strait of Hormuz, after Pakistan negotiated with Iran for the passage of several shipments through the chokepoint.
title: Another Qatar LNG Shipment Approaches Hormuz, Bound for Pakistan

description: Jerome Powell led the Fed through a pandemic and economic shutdown, but it's his resistance to political pressure that will shape his legacy. Bloomberg's Amara Omeokwe explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Jerome Powell: The Fed Chair Who Fought Back

author: Patpicha Tanakasempipat, Anuchit Nguyen
description: Thailand’s main opposition parties are seeking a court ruling on the legality of Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s plan to borrow 400 billion baht ($12 billion) to deal with the fallout of the Middle East conflict and ease the cost-of-living crisis.
title: Thai Opposition Seeks Court Ruling on $12 Billion Borrowing Plan

author: Peter Martin
description: The body of one of two US Army service members who went missing in Morocco during a military exercise has been recovered and identified, the US Army said.
title: US Army Identifies Soldier Found Dead During Morocco Exercise

author: Salma El Wardany, Galit Altstein
description: The US and Iran remain far apart on a framework to end their war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with President Donald Trump calling the Islamic Republic’s reply to his proposed peace plan unworkable.
title: US, Iran Wrangle Over Terms of Deal to End War And Reopen Hormuz

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. 

On today's show, US President Donald Trump and Iran have rejected each other’s latest peace proposals to end the 10-week conflict as the two sides struggle to maintain a fragile ceasefire.”

Beijing has officially announced the date of Donald Trump's state visit this week, publicly green-lighting the first US presidential trip to China in nearly a decade. President Trump will meet Xi Jinping on Thursday.

And the UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer will make a last-ditch effort to save his premiership on Monday morning with a politically charged address designed to hold back calls for a change in leadership atop Britain’s governing Labour Party.

Today's guest: Joe Twyman, Deltapoll, Co-Founder; Freya Beamish, TS Lombard, Chief Economist; Baiba Braže, Latvian Foreign Minister. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump Rejects Iran Latest Offer & Trump-Xi Summit | Daybreak Europe 5/11/2026

author: Jaehyun Eom
description: South Korean Finance Minister Koo Yun Cheol said he expects the country’s economic growth to exceed 2% this year, supported by surging global demand for semiconductors.
title: South Korean Finance Minister Says Growth to Exceed 2% This Year

author: Thomas Escritt
description: Hungary will no longer wield its veto on European Union policy as an instrument of blackmail and will work to win back the trust of EU and NATO partners, new Foreign Minister Anita Orban said.
title: Hungary Won’t Blackmail EU With Veto, New Foreign Minister Says

description: Joe Twyman, co-founder of the public opinion consultancy Deltapoll says UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s resignation seems inevitable “at some time because the weight of inertia is simply so strong and the performance in the council elections was so difficult”. Labour suffered a sweeping defeat in local elections on Thursday. Twyman says the results set out “in black and white” how difficult the situation is for the ruling Labour Party. Twyman says none of the front runners to replace Starmer “r
title: Starmer’s Resignation ‘Inevitable’: Pollster Joe Twyman

author: Candido Mendes
description: Angolan leader João Lourenço informed the ruling Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola that he plans to seek another term as party chief before his second presidential term ends in 2027, Jornal de Angola reported.
title: Angolan President Seeks New Ruling-Party Term, Jornal Reports

author: Oliver Crook, Aaron Eglitis
description: Latvia would welcome more US soldiers on its soil, Foreign Minister Baiba Braze said after the administration of President Donald Trump announced it will withdraw thousands of troops from Germany.
title: Latvia Would Welcome More US Troops, Foreign Minister Says

author: Weilun Soon
description: Geolocation data for some ships in the Persian Gulf showed locations and speeds that defied logic, pointing to an increase in signal interference following fresh attacks by Iran on neighboring countries.
title: Ships’ Signals Go Haywire as Hormuz Strait Tensions Escalate

description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer's political problems have likely grown too big to solve with a single speech. For now, he will try to forestall an immediate challenge to his job. Starmer will make a last-ditch effort to save his premiership on Monday morning with a politically charged address designed to hold back calls for a change in leadership atop Britain's governing Labour Party.  James Woolcock joins Stephen Carroll and Caroline Hepker on Bloomberg Radio with the details. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Preview Of Keir Starmer's Make Or Break Speech

author: Tracy Withers
description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon has ruled out a grand coalition between his National Party and the main opposition Labour Party after November’s election.
title: New Zealand PM Luxon Rules Out Grand Coalition With Labour

author: Jenny Leonard
description: Amid a hotly contested global race for minerals, a mining project in Slovakia illustrates the EU’s struggle to get its act together.
title: Race for Critical Minerals Leaves EU Struggling to Keep Up

description: President Donald Trump and Iran rejected each other’s latest peace proposals to end the 10-week conflict as the two sides struggle to maintain a fragile ceasefire. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports from Dubai. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Rejects New Iran Peace Offer as ‘Totally Unacceptable’

author: Ditas B Lopez, Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: Philippines’ Vice President Sara Duterte is facing a second impeachment as soon as Monday, a possible victory for her ally-turned-rival President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. that will likely deepen the country’s political and economic turmoil.
title: Philippine Vice President Duterte Facing Second Impeachment Vote

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Vignesh Radhakrishnan, Shruti Srivastava
description: An analysis of voting trends shows India’s leader is seeing success at uniting the Hindu majority.
title: Resurgent Modi Paves Way to Keep Power in India Well Beyond 2030

author: Heesu Lee
description: South Korea said a fire aboard a Korean-operated cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz was caused by external strikes, the first official acknowledgment by Seoul that the incident was the result of an attack, though it stopped short of assigning blame.
title: Seoul Confirms Strike on Vessel in Hormuz Before Pentagon Talks
